chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Saqr al-Sa'igh narrated to us, saying: Isa ibn Muhammad al-Alawi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Salam al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Hasan ibn Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, saying: al-Harith ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Isma'il ibn Sadaqa narrated to us, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them.

He said: When this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'And We have enumerated everything in a Clear Imam' [36:12], Abu Bakr and Umar rose from their sitting place and said: O Messenger of Allah, is it the Torah? He said: No. They said: Then is it the Gospel? He said: No. They said: Then is it the Quran? He said: No. He said: Then the Commander of the Believers, Ali (peace be upon him), approached, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: It is him. Indeed, he is the Imam in whom Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, enumerated the knowledge of everything.
ai.seo_question: Who is the 'Clear Imam' mentioned in Surah Ya-Sin verse 12?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, this hadith presents a distinct Shia interpretation of Surah Ya-Sin 36:12, identifying the 'Clear Imam' not as a scripture but as Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib. The narrative highlights the companions' initial confusion and the Prophet's clarification that divine omniscience is preserved within the Imam, establishing him as the living repository of all knowledge.
